title: The harness and the baseline
why: Open 1 (four probe modes, the verify set and the pop cases are the spec's, each run as a proto on main by the spec step; whether setUp is exported or moved is the one choice), New 1 (shots.mjs's modes and the protos are the pattern), Miss 1 (the baseline must reproduce hits.txt and pop.txt, and --diff against main must read 0%), Reach 1 (onScreen honours noCull; shots.mjs splits). An easel at 4: Haiku high. It waits on the verify set shot and timed on three trees (21 views each, about 5 s a view). About 6 files, 350 lines: shots-probe.mjs (new, about 220), shots.mjs (export and --time verify), shots-views.mjs (VERIFY, POPS), map/view.js (one line), engine/CLAUDE.md, baseline.md with its raw .txt files.

title: The frame under the bar
why: Open 2 (the bar and the proof are exact: every verify view within max(1.5x pre-art, 8) ms and every shot byte-identical to main's; the method is a search among culling by tile, caching scaled images and positions, or a wider static cache), New 1 (edges.js already culls by drawn rectangle; the rest adapts it), Miss 1 (--diff at 0% and --cull catch a moved pixel; --time and --layers measure the gain), Reach 2 (the static layer every pan redraws). An easel at 6: Sonnet medium. Settled to an exact done here rather than left to the canvas, so the canvas judges on a map that pans within the bar. About 5 files, 200 lines: layers/edges.js, woods.js, ridges.js, maybe view.js and atlas.js, frame.md and frame.txt.

title: The illustrated map, fixed and judged beside the pre-art page
why: Open 4 (a stack and a crowd kept in their hex, each layer's cull reach, and every unit, place and clan reading in its civ's colour at four zooms as well as on the pre-art page, the scout's banner at k 5: judged by eye with --hits, --pop and --units as floors), New 1 (the layers' tables and the atlas tool are the easels' and #443-#445's), Miss 3 (only the captures on the retro maps show a smudged figure or a buried overlay), Reach 2 (units, clans, places and the cull every frame draws). A canvas at 10: Sonnet high, as #440-#445's. About 8 files and 18 committed PNGs, 250 lines: layers/units.js, clans.js, places.js, centres.js and the onScreen callers, view.js, maybe sources.js and the atlas, views.md, shots/.

title: Review the piece
why: The goal is judged by eye on identical views of three trees, and main may move under the piece (gameplay PRs land beside the art track), so Opus medium. It checks no Rust moved, runs every shots check and the controls, times the verify set against the pre-art page, reads the triples at each zoom, clicks stacked units, a crowded town's clan, a capital and a settlement on the page, pans a stack across the edge, and puts the captures and tables in the PR.
